comment: The CLIs the copilot can be, and what they offer before they are asked. Shared because both processes need it: electron/ai.js decides what it will spawn, src/models.js decides what the dropdown shows, and two copies of that is how the two disagree. Same arrangement as vault-contract.json and zoom-steps.json. `command` is the binary spawned — one process per turn, with the vault as its working directory. There is no HTTP client here and no key of ours to keep: a gateway (OpenRouter, z.ai) is reached by configuring it inside opencode, where its key already lives. The `fallbacks` below are what the dropdown shows before the CLIs have been asked — a seed, not a limit, because both of these catalogues are account properties this file cannot check a name against, so what the panel offers is what gets spawned. A devin id carries `{effort}` where the reasoning level goes: devin spells the level into the model name rather than taking it as a flag, and `startDevinTurn` fills the slot from whatever the effort slider says. `offerByDefault` is false for opencode alone — its four hundred-odd entries are what the Models-offered setting exists to keep out of the dropdown. `auth` is the argument list that answers whether the CLI is signed in. `grants` is what each CLI can actually do in the read-only or write-capable provider mode, in the user's words: neither takes a per-tool allowlist, so each is fenced only by that mode — the UI's Ask and Auto choices decide whether write access is confirmed first.

grants.write: read, edit and create notes, and run shell commands inside the vault
